source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 1. Bios Setting EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’] EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled 2. Deploy Intel ITP environment. 3. Boot SUT into shell 4. Execute Intel Cscripts on client 5. Using folling command >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log") >>>halt() >>>ei.injectThreeStrike(socket, port) >>>go 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Socket 0~N (Intel Three-Strike timeout on Socket 0~N error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'three.strike|timeout|MCE_|machine.check'; echo __Three-Strike_timeout_on_Socket_0~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

disposition_reason: Three-Strike is distinguished by a catastrophic timeout path whose service interruption is expected, so availability of SSH after injection is not a safe control or primary oracle. The test must separate autonomous reboot from operator recovery with an external timeline and maximum wait; otherwise both an immediate manual reset and an indefinite hang could be misreported as success. A CPU-over-temperature display is not self-evidently caused by a UPI timeout and needs a platform event-map justification. Exact FAE tooling and human control make the case conditionally executable, while the agent must never initiate or repeat the outage. test_case.purpose: Trigger the Intel Three-Strike timeout at each approved socket/port, confirm the expected catastrophic crash/hang and automatic recovery path, and correlate CPU/UPI fatal evidence across BMC, UEFI, OS and physical indicators.
required_package: Supported platform/CPU/socket-port mapping and Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash
Approved injectThreeStrike semantics and exact catastrophic signatures
Maximum crash/hang and automatic-reboot windows plus independent console/power timeline
Front-panel/LCD applicability and reason CPU Over Temp represents this stimulus
Vendor recovery, post-recovery health and BIOS restoration procedure
test_case.test_command: On a dedicated SUT, an FAE/operator enables the exact EDKII controls, validates the socket/port, performs one approved Three-Strike injection and starts an independent timeline. The operator waits the specified autonomous-reboot interval, avoids premature power intervention, then follows the vendor recovery boundary, collects BMC/UEFI/OS and front-panel/LCD artifacts and restores settings.
